cells.tense: Right now, what you want and what you're doing point the same way, and it carries you without strain.
cells.act: let the satisfaction of a finished thing land
cells.ask: Spend ten minutes with something you finished recently and receive it — the satisfaction, unhurried. Don't touch the next thing. Stay with what's done.
cells.core:
You're moving through unclear ground, and what you want and what you're doing are pointed the same way. That's rarer than it sounds. The fog doesn't lift, but you don't need it to — enough is lit for the next step, and you take it without having to argue yourself into it. That's why it doesn't burn. Some of this came from things you already lived through; the dreaming runs clean because the experience behind it got digested instead of shelved.

The risk now is sliding to the next thing before this one is received. Sit with a finished thing for ten minutes and receive it — the satisfaction, unhurried, no improving it. Deep satisfaction is yours to feel, and it's the fuel that keeps the walk steady when the fog thickens again.
cells.sheetLine: The walk is easy because you're not fighting yourself.
cells.verb: letting will and feeling move the same direction until the effort stops feeling like effort

cells.tense: You're braced for a version of this that hasn't arrived yet, and the bracing makes the fog feel like a threat.
cells.act: gather the scattered thoughts into one line
cells.ask: Put the loose pieces on one page, then draw a single line through them giving the next move. One line, not a plan. Let it be enough.
cells.core:
Unclear ground is where you live right now, and the strain has tipped: instead of taking the lit step, you're trying to see the whole road at once. What's coming gets rehearsed, plans made for versions of the situation that don't exist yet. The drive is still there, but it's pushing against the fog instead of walking through it. Feeling and will are out of step — one is racing ahead, one is still here.

More looking won't fix this. Gather the scattered pieces and put them into one line. One page, then one line through it: this is what gets done next. The line doesn't have to be right, it has to be one. The fog clears a little around a single declared step, not around a full map.
cells.sheetLine: The fog isn't the problem. Racing it is.

cells.tense: You're past a threshold you're still standing at, and the fog you face is the one after it.
cells.ask: Name three things the last change produced — a skill, a person, a way of working — and put them where you'll see them. Use one this week.
cells.core:
Something ended or shifted, and you haven't arrived on the other side of it. The fog here isn't the usual kind — you're not unsure about the next step, you're still turned toward a door that's already closed. There isn't enough light to move because you haven't taken in what the last stretch gave you. The pull is quiet, and the doing feels like going through motions.

What fills this is not forcing feeling into the fog. Gather what the change grew. Name what the ending produced, put it somewhere visible, and use one piece of it this week. That's how the light comes back — not by deciding to feel motivated, but by handling real yield until it's worth walking toward.

cells.tense: You are steering through this fog, and your account of it says the path is doing the steering.
cells.act: keep building the thing with sustained craft
cells.ask: Open the thing you keep returning to and do today's ten minutes deliberately, as a choice. Mark that you chose it, and continue.
cells.core:
In this fog, the next step gets found — and it gets found by you. You've been doing it a while: reading what's ahead, adjusting, keeping the thing moving. If someone asked, you'd say the path revealed itself, or the work just needed doing. Both are true enough, and both leave out the hand on it.

The way back in is to keep building, knowingly. Take the thing you return to and do today's part of it deliberately — not because the path asked, but because you did. This is not insight arriving; it's craft, persisted in, and saying so is the whole difference. What you call the road is you walking it.
cells.sheetLine: The path is revealing itself because you're reading it.
